questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been in love with Italy, which was my main motivation - 2 of my priorities were in Italy (Bologna and Milano). I didn't know much about Milano University beforehand other than their large amount of foreign students, which of course opens up the possibility of cultural exchange across borders. I have since learned that Milano University is held in high esteem both nationally and internationally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy, with emails sent by the international office guiding me in the right direction, and answers to my explanatory emails. Milano University's webpages are somewhat easy to navigate, so applying for new courses (the courses I had chosen had scheduling conflicts or weren't offered in the Autumn semester) was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Emails to and from the International Office. 

YesMilano also have great guides. I don't quite remember who led me to them, maybe that was ESN Milano Statale.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of offers (on Idealista etc.) that are only for long-term (more than 6 months) so that can be an issue. However it was my roommate who found our accommodation which was posted in the ESN Milano Statale WhatsApps group. 

So it can be difficult, and some did report that some sites will try to scam you so looking out for that is generally advisable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Lok out for potential scams, always see the housing before you pay and so on. 

Start looking for housing accommodation early. Can save a lot of stress.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
After getting access to Unimia and MyAriel (the main webpages for students at Milano University), registering for courses is quite easy. The second box on the Unimia site is for Course Registration that also includes a guide. It is also quite easy to modify study plans. 
Finding details about courses is quite easy to find on MyAriel.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other than the guide on the site itself, the International Office also sent a guide (that was, as I recall, the same guide).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I did have to change some of my courses while in Milano, but it all worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guide, don't be afraid to change courses if there are scheduling conflicts or other issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were Master level courses, with course literature etc. suitable for the level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not too different, lots of class lectures. More student presentations than I am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Ontology 
Philosophical Analysis
Language and Metaphysics 
Human Resource Management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The best course I had was Advanced Ontology, so if future exchange students are interested in philosophy this course is recommendable.

questions.answer: Buying groceries is definitely cheaper than in Copenhagen, but other than that, prices are fairly similar.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really search for such activities provided by my host institution, and instead searched for opportunities outside of my host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: For weekends and holidays, there are a wide arrange of museums, beautiful places in the city and a lot of churches so that is some things to do. Visiting other parts of Northern Italy (personally went to Cremona, and has a visit to Como and Bologna planned). Plenty of nice cafés and bars to hang around in, get a coffee or an aperitivo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, I somewhat feel at home in Italian milieus.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
ESN Milano Statale has a lot of social events. Also spontaneous invitations on their Whatsapp group can also appear.  
I would also recommend drinking a coffee or an aperitivo after class with your classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Italian café culture and their general openness and curiosity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Dress for the occasion - the weather in Milano goes from freezing/near freezing in the Winter, to 30+ degrees in summer and early autumn. So a wide arrange of clothing is recommendable. 
2. Never be afraid to ask for help or directions, Italians - Milanese included - are very friendly. 
3. Remember to enjoy yourself outside of academia. Milano has plenty to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Within Academia it was all the new knowledge I learned - analytical philosophy (which my philosophical courses were) is completely new to me. 
Outside of Academia it was all the interesting people I met. From locals to other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The course Advanced Ontology.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
